name: keendreams
title: Keen Dreams (id Software / Softdisk, Borland C++ / DOS)
_doc: THE FIRST 16-BIT TARGET, and it is not expected to build yet. PRISM emits for i386 and only for i386; this program is Borland C++ real mode, with 242 `far` declarations and 141 uses of MK_FP/FP_SEG/FP_OFF/_seg/int86 across its C. It is here to be a MEASUREMENT: a build that fails loudly names what a 16-bit backend has to supply, which is cheaper and truer than estimating it. gate-abi16 and gate-bits16 already pin the layout rules against Open Watcom for exactly this day.
_why_this_one: Chosen over Wolf3D, Catacomb 3D and Hovertank 3D, and the first version of this note chose it on HALF the evidence: it counted .ASM files and missed the inline assembly inside the C, which the second build then stopped on. Re-measured with both halves -- .ASM lines / C-visible entry points / inline asm statements / segment-register touches: KeenDreams 3,802 / 25 / 640 / 95; Wolf3D 1,951 / 18 / 1,127 / 247; Catacomb3D 4,159 / 37 / 1,288 / 276; Hovertank3D 14,685 / 202 / 373 / 64. On raw assembly VOLUME Wolf3D is now the smaller. What still puts Keen Dreams first is the NATURE of it: the fewest segment-register touches of the three whose files are tractable, and .ASM entry points that are ordinary routines (VW_Plot, VW_DrawTile8, RFL_UpdateTiles...) where Wolf3D's include three timer interrupt handlers and self-modifying 386 detection. The resemblance to Jump 'n Bump's get_block/put_block holds for those files ONLY: inline assembly is interleaved with C inside function bodies and cannot be bound as a separate function. That is the hard part, for all four.
_units: The program's own list, read out of kdreams.prj -- a binary Borland project whose file names sit in it as plain text. Worth the trouble: the tree also carries lscr/loadscn2.c and static/makeobj.c, and the project names neither. BUT the .prj records DEPENDENCIES as well as project items, and reading every name out of it took one too many: id_us_s.c is #included by id_us.c:516, so it is part of that unit and not one of its own. Compiled alone it failed at its line 19 for want of the context id_us.c gives it, which is how the mistake showed. 17 units.
_asm: FOUR assembly objects the project builds and this target does not: id_vw_a.asm, id_vw_ae.asm, id_rf_a.asm, id_us_a.asm. They are MASM/TASM, read by src/asm/tasm.js and translated by src/asm/tasm16.js (gate-tasm-front, gate-tasm-run) but not yet bound into this build -- which still reports their symbols as undefined. id_vw_ac.asm is in the tree and NOT in the project: it is the CGA variant, and GRMODE in id_heads.h ships as EGAGR. Selecting neither: EGA is what the tree already says.
_static_data: make.bat runs static/makeobj.c over the .KDR files in static/ to produce KDREDICT.OBJ and KDREHEAD.OBJ, which the project LINKS. PRISM links no object files, so that data has no route in today. Named here rather than discovered later.
_first_gap: MEASURED TWICE. First stop: ID_MM.H:43, `typedef void _seg * memptr;` -- Borland's segment pointer, a pointer kind rather than a qualifier. The parser now accepts _seg and huge immediately before a star and marks the pointer; any function that reaches one is refused by name, and any sizeof/offsetof/_Alignof of a type holding one is refused rather than folded (types.js segPtr explains why the placeholder size cannot be left undefined). Second stop: kd_play.c:592, `asm mov es,[WORD PTR mapsegs+4]` -- Borland's statement form of inline assembly. 640 such statements in 11 of this program's 20 C files, 95 of them touching a segment register directly. kd_main.c and kd_demo.c parse whole.
_caseInsensitive: id_us.c includes "ID_US_S.c" and the file is id_us_s.c. It resolved here only because this machine's filesystem ignores case; on Linux it would not. DOS never had to care.
_survey: SURVEYED UNIT BY UNIT, because one build stops at the first failure and the survey is the point. ALL 17 UNITS NOW COMPILE (id_ca.c since compile.ppSizeof, see _ppSizeof); what follows is the history of the one that did not, which was then a DECISION rather than a gap: id_ca.c:1471, `#if BUFFERSIZE < sizeof(maptype)`, refused by name and staying refused -- sizeof in a preprocessor condition is Borland's, not C's, every conforming compiler rejects that file, and the #if sits inside a function body so there is not even a valid partial unit to read types from. It guards a compile-time assertion whose body is an English sentence, the idiom that predates #error, and it is the only occurrence in the corpus. Cleared, each with its own gate: NULL in kd_keen.c and kd_act1.c, from <STDIO.H> and friends written in capitals (gate-include-case); `static void interrupt` in id_in.c and id_sd.c (gate-borland16); a lone 0x1A in the file id_us.c includes, the DOS end-of-file marker, this being the only built target whose sources carry one (gate-dos-eof); `boolean inline = false;` in kd_act2.c, a C99 keyword five years early (gate-c89-inline); and kd_play.c's locationless `#`, which was a `#pragma warn -pro` sitting between an `else` and the statement it governs -- legal C anywhere, and the one of three pragma positions the parser did not step over (gate-pragma-position). Truly absent, and still reported: alloc.h, mem.h, process.h. THE PARSER IS NO LONGER THE SUBJECT. What the 16 that parse are refused FOR, under dos16m, after `_seg` pointers (gate-segptr) took the count from 144 functions to 81 and Borland inline assembly (gate-borlandasm) from 81 to 58, the DOS interrupt surface (env `borland`, gate-dosint) from 58 to 33, cast lvalues (gate-castlvalue) to 26, `huge` (gate-huge) to 21 and the Borland library (gate-borlandlib) to 5 -- every one of the five refused on purpose: gametext, data in a static .OBJ; sys_errlist, whose wording is Borland's; and three register reads only Borland's machine could answer -- the timer ISR reading the interrupted loop's CX, the critical-error handler reading DOS's DI, and MML_CheckForEMS taking OFFSET of a local -- the pseudo-registers _AX/_AH/_AL/_ES/_CX with getvect/setvect/poke/harderr. Those three, and a 16-bit backend to put under them.
_compile: No compiler identity macro is tested anywhere in the source and no #pragma pack or option appears, so the memory model is entirely a Borland project setting rather than anything the C states. That is itself a finding: nothing in the source tells a reader which model it wants.
_c89: Borland C++ 2.0 predates C99, and kd_act2.c:1404 uses the word: `boolean inline = false;`, then assigns to it and tests it. The flag gives `inline` back as an identifier and nothing else -- the GNU spellings __inline and __inline__ stay keywords, and no program here uses restrict or _Bool as a name.
_model: dos16m, the MEDIUM model -- the one the program declares in its own assembly: `MODEL MEDIUM,C` in id_rf_a.asm and id_us_a.asm, which must match the C it links with. Far code, four-byte function pointers; near data, two-byte data pointers; `far` and `near` honoured wherever they are written (gate-abi16m, against Watcom -mm). DGROUP sits at linear 0 so a near pointer and its linear address are the same number; the near statics end at 0xBE41 and the seven far objects that are defined -- son, prnt, freq, text_buf, d_code, d_len, mmblocks -- live from 0x10000 (gate-farobj). Of the twelve the source declares far, story, gametext and maphead are externs defined in the static-data .OBJ files PRISM does not link, and p_len and p_code sit inside `#if INCLUDE_LZH_COMP`, which is 0. HISTORY: this target was briefly dos16l, on a deduction from the size of its statics that had been measured in i386 type sizes; it is retracted in the commit that found MODEL MEDIUM. run() executes it since argv, variadic arguments and the runtime's pointer and int stores are sized by the model (gate-dos16-run, whole programs against Borland C++ 2.0 running them with this target's options).
_layout: THE COMPILER OPTIONS ARE READ FROM THE PROGRAM'S OWN PROJECT, by Borland's own tool: PRJCFG (Borland C++ 3.1, archive.org bcpp31) run in DOSBox-X on the unmodified kdreams.prj writes the BCC options it records -- -mm -a -K, and no -b- (goldens/borland-prj.json, tools/gate-borland-options.mjs). Meanings and defaults from BCC's own help: -mm the medium model; -a word alignment, which is the 16-bit tables' alignment of 2; -K "default char is unsigned"; -b* "treat enums as integers" is a DEFAULT, so enums are int-sized. Hence model dos16m, signedChar FALSE, enums 'int'. PRJCFG 3.1 is believed on a 2.0 project because on Hovertank 3-D its output agrees with that program's compiler-GENERATED assembly on three settings (no -K and cbw; -a and pad bytes; no -m and MODEL SMALL), checked by the same gate. CORRECTION: the commit before this one set signedChar TRUE, inferred from Hovertank's generated code; Keen's project differs from Hovertank's on exactly that option. WHAT THESE DECIDE: under -a and int enums only ffblk's sizeof depends on alignment, and objtype (76 bytes), which kd_demo.c writes raw to disk, is laid out as Borland laid it out; the char sign changes the code of 24 of 402 emitted functions.
_ppSizeof: id_ca.c:1471 is `#if BUFFERSIZE < sizeof(maptype)`, inside `#ifdef MAPHEADERLINKED` -- which id_ca.h:37 defines, so the condition IS evaluated -- guarding a compile-time assertion whose body is an English sentence. Borland preprocessed and parsed in one pass and could answer it; a standalone preprocessor cannot. compile.ppSizeof STATES the answer, as an option and not a source change: maptype is 38 bytes. tools/gate-pp-sizeof.mjs holds the number to two references -- PRISM's own layout of maptype under this target's options, and Borland C++ 2.0's, measured by running it (goldens/borland-layout.json) -- so it cannot drift from either. 0x1000 < 38 is false, the sentence is skipped, and the unit compiles. HISTORY: this was a refusal by name, decided when no oracle could vouch for the number.
_tasm: The Turbo Assembler modules the project links (id_vw_a.asm includes id_vw_ae.asm, GRMODE being EGAGR), read by src/asm/tasm.js, translated by src/asm/tasm16.js and bound by src/asm/tasm-link.js: their _DATA in DGROUP with its publics (px, py, fontcolor, pdrawmode, bufferwidth, bufferheight, shifttabletable), their code in far memory, each public PROC a C function under Borland's calling convention.
_dataObjects: Transcribed from static/make.bat and static/makeobj.c, which turn each file into an .OBJ: mode c puts the bytes in _DATA of DGROUP (near), mode f in a paragraph-aligned FAR_DATA segment of its own; the public is the given name, or `_` and the lower-case file name when none is given (context, gametext, story). The C symbol drops Borland's leading underscore. PIRACY.SCN becomes piracy.h, which kd_main.c includes only under #if 0. The files come from the source tree at build time; none enters this repository.
